title: Filling a prime grid that starts with three hundred and forty three
description: A three by three grid has row products three hundred and forty three, sixty six and forty four, and column products twenty eight, one hundred and fifty four and two hundred and thirty one. The row of three sevens opens the grid, and the rest follows by dividing by seven.
teaching_notes: One idea: a product that is one prime used three times fills a whole line at once, and dividing the column products by that prime leaves pairs to place. Watch for students who place the pairs without checking the row products.

video_script.why: The child spots the product made of one prime, fills that row, divides each column product by the prime, and places each pair using the row products.
video_script.substitution: Fill the row made of one prime, divide each column product by it, then place each pair using the row products.
video_script.anchor: an empty 3 by 3 grid with 343, 66 and 44 at the right of the rows and 28, 154 and 231 below the columns
video_script.payoff_line: The rows are seven, seven, seven, then two, eleven, three, then two, two, eleven

final_answer.spoken: the rows are seven, seven, seven, then two, eleven, three, then two, two, eleven

maths_rules: 343 = 7 x 7 x 7, so the top row is 7, 7, 7
each column has a 7 on top, so the two cells below make the column product divided by 7: 28 / 7 = 4 = 2 x 2, 154 / 7 = 22 = 2 x 11, 231 / 7 = 33 = 3 x 11
the first column is 2 and 2, so both lower rows start with 2
66 = 2 x 3 x 11 and has a 2, so 3 and 11 are left; the middle column holds 2 and 11, so 11 goes in the second row; the right column holds 3 and 11, so 3 goes in the second row and 11 in the third row
44 = 2 x 2 x 11, so the third row is 2, 2, 11
video_script.design: One idea: fill the row made of one prime, divide each column product by it, and place the pairs with the row products. Callback to the all-fives column of the earlier puzzle. Wrong idea: none is broken. The grid stays on the board to the end.
